subfield: Condensed matter and materials physics for energy conversion
motivation: Miyasaka first used organometal halide perovskites as light absorbers in photovoltaic cells (2009). Park and Snaith, working independently in 2012, turned them into solid-state devices. Park introduced the solid-state sensitized perovskite cell. Snaith showed that perovskites carry charge over long distances as ambipolar semiconductors, which made thin-film planar devices possible. Their discovery uncovered a new class of solution-processable semiconductors with remarkable physics: sharp absorption edges, long carrier diffusion lengths, defect tolerance and tunable bandgaps. Within about fifteen years, power-conversion efficiencies rose from under 4% to above 26%, and perovskite–silicon tandems now exceed 33%, beyond the single-junction silicon limit. Operando synchrotron and neutron studies of their ionic and structural dynamics have opened a broad research field across physics, chemistry and engineering. Commercial tandem modules are now emerging. This work has changed both semiconductor physics and the outlook for low-cost solar energy in the energy transition.
